sections.presenting_complaint: Diabetes review following a hypoglycaemic episode.
sections.history: Episode about three months ago after skipping lunch while gardening: sweaty, shaky, confused. Daughter (who has type 1 diabetes) found him confused, measured capillary glucose 2.8 mmol/L and treated with juice and biscuits; recovered within 15 minutes. Not driving at the time. Occasional pre-meal wobbliness. Drives locally. No neuropathic symptoms. No visual problems; retinal screening due. Attended with daughter.
sections.medications_allergies: Metformin 1 g twice daily. Gliclazide 80 mg twice daily. Atorvastatin 20 mg. Ramipril 5 mg. No known drug allergies.
sections.examination: Pedal pulses palpable. Ankle brachial pressure index 1.0 bilaterally. Monofilament sensation normal in both feet. Callus under the right first metatarsal head. BP 138/84. Weight 91 kg. Bloods: HbA1c 62 mmol/mol (previously 58), eGFR 52 (stable).
sections.impression: Type 2 diabetes with recent hypoglycaemia on gliclazide; HbA1c above target. Stable CKD stage 3a. Low-risk foot with callus.
sections.plan: Continue gliclazide 80 mg twice daily. Start empagliflozin 10 mg once daily; sick day rules explained and leaflet given. Podiatry referral for callus. Book retinal screening. Review in 3 months with HbA1c and renal function.
sections.safety_netting: Check blood glucose before driving and every 2 hours on long journeys; do not drive if below 5 mmol/L; keep fast-acting glucose in the car. Severe hypo (needed help from someone else): if another within 12 months, or any hypo while driving, stop driving and inform the DVLA. Stop empagliflozin if vomiting, diarrhoea or unable to eat and drink.
